paper.citation: Athey, S., Tibshirani, J. and Wager, S. (2019). Generalized random forests. The Annals of Statistics 47(2), 1148-1178. DOI: 10.1214/18-AOS1709.
paper.source_locator: Section 6.2 'Example: Causal Forests', arXiv:1610.01271v4 (5 Apr 2018) PDF pp.22-23: the section opens on p.22; the working equations tau(x) and e(x) = (1/4)(1 + beta_{2,4}(x3)), m(x) = 2 x3 - 1, the sentence defining the third setting ('We also consider a third setting with both heterogeneity and confounding, that combines tau(.) from the first setting with m(.) and e(.) from the second') and Table 1 all appear on p.23. The settings are unnumbered prose, so the locator gives page + paragraph instead of an equation number.

mechanism.name: Athey-Tibshirani-Wager (2019) third setting: heterogeneity and confounding combined

generation_equations.label: Outcome
generation_equations.expression: Y = m(X) + A tau(X) + eps, eps ~ Normal(0,1)

assumptions: SUTVA: one version of treatment, no interference
Unconfoundedness: treatment depends on X3, which also enters the baseline m(X) = 2 X3 - 1, so the design is observational
Overlap: 0.25 <= e(X) <= 0.777 because 20 u (1-u)^3 peaks at u = 1/4
Homoscedastic Gaussian noise with unit variance

properties.notes: Three active coordinates: X1, X2 carry a multiplicative sigmoid effect, X3 drives both the propensity and the baseline. X4, X5 are inert. The interaction is the product s(X1)s(X2); nonlinearity comes from the sigmoid and from the quartic propensity.

estimand.name: tau(x0) = E[Y(1) - Y(0) | X = x0]
estimand.definition: Conditional average treatment effect at the declared query points for the combined setting: sigmoid-product heterogeneity on X1, X2 together with a beta-density propensity and a linear baseline on X3.

truth.expression: Conditional average treatment effect at the declared query points for the combined setting: sigmoid-product heterogeneity on X1, X2 together with a beta-density propensity and a linear baseline on X3.
truth.derivation: Closed form: tau(x0) = s(x1) s(x2) with s the source sigmoid; the confounding variables do not enter the effect, so the value can be compared directly with the randomised sibling contribution.

adaptations: Ambient dimension fixed at p = 5 instead of the source's p in {10, 20}; the third setting needs only X1, X2 (effect) and X3 (confounding).
The source writes Y ~ N(m(X) + (W - 0.5) tau(X), 1); this package uses A in {0,1} and Y = m(X) + A tau(X) + eps with eps ~ N(0,1). The CATE is unchanged.

The effect surface is identical to cate-wager-2018-sigmoid-product-v1 because the source builds the third setting by reusing tau from its first setting; the difference between the two contributions is the confounding structure, which is the point of this row of Table 1.
The source aggregates over 60 replications with B = 2000 trees; no forest is fitted here.
